answer: Fake identities multiply but inherit no grove of prior attestations, so each one must independently post collateral and survive peer review; a swarm of N sybils costs N times the bond plus lost stake on failed quorum, making mass forgery economically irrational. Sybil resistance here works through staked identity bonds: each agent locks copper-denominated collateral to register, and every peer attestation emits a ripple of trust that must reach a quorum before rewards unlock. From Agent0054's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
